provenance: And four people — Francis Bechtel, Jacob Klein, Chantel Ramirez and Denise Johnson — put their names on a complaint against the California Department of Water Resources, on behalf of everybody who had been ordered out, asking for the out-of-pocket cost of the two days and the loss of use of their homes for the two days.

text: That is the entire claim. Not the dam. Not the crisis. Not damages for fear. Expenses, for two days.

text: A class action is for a harm small enough that no single person could sensibly litigate it, spread across enough people that it adds up to something real.
provenance: A class action is a device for a particular kind of problem: a harm small enough that no single person could sensibly litigate it, spread across enough people that it adds up to something real. Two nights out of a rented house is exactly that harm. No lawyer takes that case for one person. For a hundred and eighty-eight thousand, it becomes a case.

text: But the price of using it is that the group has to be a group. A court has to be able to say, of any person, whether they are in it or out of it.
provenance: But the price of using it is that the group has to be a group. A court has to be able to say, of any person in California, whether they are in it or out of it — because a judgment binds everybody inside the definition, including people who never heard of the case.

text: Class certification was denied. On the fifteenth of March, twenty twenty-two, the Third District Court of Appeal affirmed.
provenance: Class certification was denied. It was denied to the Bechtel plaintiffs, and it was denied in the same ninety-page ruling to a second group of Oroville property owners, who did not appeal.
